title: OrganLens: Organ-Specific Representation Learning for CT Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2607.25164v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: A CT examination captures multiple organs, but many biomedical questions concern abnormalities, prognosis, or longitudinal change in a specific organ. These questions require a separate representation for each organ within the same CT volume. Existing CT foundation models commonly produce a single volume-level representation, while recent anatomy-aware methods either encode pre-separated organ volumes or explicitly disentangle images into organ token groups. The former may remove clinically relevant surrounding context, while the latter does not condition a shared encoder on a selected organ before its features are formed. We introduce OrganLens for organ-specific representation learning through self-supervision. An organ identity conditions a shared CT encoder, while organ-specific distillation and anatomy-mask supervision shape features for anatomy-weighted pooling into organ-specific representations. translated_title: OrganLens：面向CT基础模型的器官特异性表示学习
translated_abstract: arXiv:2607.25164v2 公告类型： replace-cross 摘要：一次CT检查会捕获多个器官，但许多生物医学问题关注的是特定器官的异常、预后或纵向变化。这些问题需要在同一CT体积内为每个器官生成独立的表示。现有的CT基础模型通常只产生单一的体积级表示，而近期的解剖感知方法要么对预先分割的器官体积进行编码，要么将图像显式解耦为器官token组。前者可能丢失临床上相关的周围上下文信息，后者则在特征形成之前无法以选定的器官为条件来约束共享编码器。我们提出了OrganLens，通过自监督学习实现器官特异性表示。器官身份作为条件来约束共享的CT编码器，同时通过器官特异性蒸馏和解剖掩码监督来塑造特征，并经解剖加权池化生成器官特异性表示。在推理阶段，共享的（摘要内容至此截断）
tldr: OrganLens提出以器官身份条件化共享CT编码器，结合器官特异性蒸馏与解剖掩码监督的自监督方法，为CT基础模型生成器官特异性表示，克服了现有模型仅有单一体积级表示的局限。
